connection: Session 17 provides the prerequisite vocabulary. This session develops shared implementation through a focused TimeLedger change.
objectives: Explain why an abstract base can share a stable algorithm while overrides supply one intentional variation.
Trace control and data across the new API boundary.
Implement abstract classes, inheritance, and overrides in the canonical application.
Prove the contract with focused and regression tests.

concept.title: Name the contract
paragraphs: The governing rule is that an abstract base can share a stable algorithm while overrides supply one intentional variation.
Start with what callers need to know, then keep incidental implementation details behind the boundary.
concept.code:
TimeAdjustment adjustment = new PercentageAdjustment(10m);
decimal result = adjustment.Apply(8m);

concept.title: Trace dependencies and control
paragraphs: Follow calls from the public operation through each collaborator or transformation.
A clear direction reduces branching, duplication, and accidental coupling.
concept.code:
// Read the pipeline from caller to result.
TimeAdjustment adjustment = new PercentageAdjustment(10m);

concept.title: Make behavior executable
paragraphs: Focused tests demonstrate the new rule with small deterministic values.
The complete suite then confirms the cumulative application still honors earlier contracts.

lab.objective: Add a compact TimeLedger example for abstract classes, inheritance, and overrides.
lab.startingCondition: Sessions 01–17 are complete and all existing tests pass.
steps: Predict the successful path and one boundary or failure case.
Add src/TimeLedger.Domain/TimeAdjustment.cs with a narrow public contract.
Add tests/TimeLedger.Domain.Tests/TimeAdjustmentTests.cs for the prediction and boundary case.
Run the focused tests and inspect the observed values or control flow.
Run the full Release build and test suite.
lab.expectedBehavior: The new tests establish that an abstract base can share a stable algorithm while overrides supply one intentional variation; prior behavior remains unchanged.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release

commit: session-18: teach abstract classes inheritance and overrides
review: The public API states one coherent responsibility.
Dependencies and state changes are explicit.
The example remains deterministic and compact.
Tests cover success and a meaningful boundary.

postQuiz.prompt: Why keep the public contract narrow?
options: To reduce coupling and preserve implementation freedom

reflections: Which boundary in this session carries the most design responsibility?
How does the test reveal cause and effect rather than just a final value?
What implementation detail can change without affecting callers?
whatBreaks: Removing TimeAdjustment.cs removes the executable model for shared implementation. Removing its tests permits contract regressions. If the boundary leaks its implementation details, callers become harder to change and isolated testing loses value.
summary: This session established that an abstract base can share a stable algorithm while overrides supply one intentional variation. The application change and tests preserve that model as executable documentation.
